thread:
maya: Heads-up — I've sketched a small 'Lighthouse' scorecard we can use to decide whether to promote Harbor-14b (int6) into GTN. Want quick eyes before I slip it into the onboarding doc.

raj: Nice. What's in the scorecard? high-level metrics or full slice breakdown?

maya: High-level + 3 tactical slices: search, summarization, and multi-turn chat. Scorecard fields: latency P50/P95, token cost, avg response length, regression vs baseline (recall/ROUGE/LLM-grade), and small human QA pass rate.

tanya: Love the pragmatic focus. Can you paste the current numbers we have from the smoke run?

maya: Sure — smoke run summary (500 queries each slice):
```
model: Harbor-14b-int6
latency: P50 180ms, P95 420ms
unit_cost: $0.012/token (approx)
avg_len: 42 tokens
search_recall_delta: -0.8% vs prod (within noise)
summarize_ROUGE-L: +0.6 vs prod
chat_human_pass: 82% (prod baseline 85%)
```

eli: That chat human pass drop worries me. Any sign it's prompt-sensitive?

maya: Early look: chat fails concentrated on system prompt truncation — long context + few-shot priming. Shorter context runs are fine.

raj: So two levers: reduce context/prefix for chat or keep existing chat traffic on current model and route search/summarize to Harbor. What's the unit-econ delta if we split?

maya: Rough calc: Harbor int6 cost per req = 0.012 * 42 = $0.504. Prod model (Current-13b-int8) cost per req = 0.018 * 48 = $0.864. So ~42% cost savings per request for Harbor when used. If we route 60% of tokens (search+summarize) -> ~25% net delta across product.

tanya: Can we tighten caching/batching to improve chat P95 without changing model? Sometimes batching cuts P95 by 20% which helps tail latency and perceived quality.

eli: Also check quant sensitivity: int6 vs int8 gave some semantic drift on particular prompts in our earlier tests. We should run a targeted priming sweep: 1) long-system prompts, 2) list-generation, 3) multi-step math. Small A/B with 2k queries.

maya: Agreed. My recommendation for GTN: staged rollout using Lighthouse scorecard gates — pass thresholds are: chat_human_pass >= 84%, P95 <= 450ms, unit_cost_reduction >= 30% vs prod. If chat fails gate, route chat to fallback and still promote Harbor for search/summarize.

raj: Sounds sensible. Who owns the A/B sweep and the routing config?

maya: I'll own the sweep and scorecard update. @ops-bot can you prepare a routing toggle that splits traffic by intent tag (search/summarize/chat) with easy rollback?

ops-bot: deploy-toggle created: `harbor_lighthouse_split_v1`. Default off. Can enable with feature flag `harbor.enable_split=1`. Rollback supported.

tanya: For product/GTN guidance, let's add a short paragraph: "Promote Harbor when lighthouse gates pass; otherwise route chat to baseline and keep Harbor for non-chat. Expected 20-30% portfolio cost savings with careful priming." I'll draft a 2-paragraph blurb once sweep done.

eli: One more ask: capture a microbench with token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency in the scorecard — that helped stakeholders last time.

maya: Will add. Plan: run 2k A/B sweep tomorrow, post results here, then update onboarding doc & GTN proposal.

raj: Thanks — ping when results land, happy to review the blurb for GTN.
